title: Residue field of a point of a fibre product
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with fibre product $X\times_SY$ and projections $p,q$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $z\in X\times_SY$, put $x=p(z)$, $y=q(z)$, $s=f(x)=g(y)$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be the kernel of the ring map $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto p^\sharp(a)q^\sharp(b)$, where $p^\sharp:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$, $q^\sharp:\kappa(y)\to\kappa(z)$ are the maps induced by $p$ and $q$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] (this $\mathfrak p$ is the prime ideal attached to $z$ in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]). Then the induced field homomorphism from the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of $\mathfrak p$ (the fraction field of $(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y))/\mathfrak p$) to $\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism; it is compatible with the maps from $\kappa(x)$ and from $\kappa(y)$. In particular, if $(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y))/\mathfrak p$ is a field, then $(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y))/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism of extensions of $\kappa(x)$ and of $\kappa(y)$.
